svg.aria-label: Jewelry outer shipping box rules: right-size to inner box plus dunnage, under 1 lb and under 10 inches is the cheapest carrier tier

g.text: Right-sizing the outer box
Most jewelry ships well under 1 lb and under 10 inches per side — the cheapest rate tier at every major carrier
outer box — one size up from the inner box
inner fitted box
≈1″ dunnage
≈1″ dunnage
plain brown box — no jewelry brand name on the label
The cheap tier is structural, not lucky
A ring or necklace box “ships in a box well under 1 lb and under
10 inches on any side” — savings come from right-sizing the outer
box, not from downgrading the protective layers.
Carrier rules rule out padded envelopes
FedEx explicitly requires corrugated packaging for jewelry shipments
and prohibits padded mailers for declared values over $500 —
mailers offer no compression protection at all.
Insurance and signature tiers (USPS, published)
$100 included with Priority / Ground Advantage · standard coverage
to about $5,000 · Registered Mail to $50,000 from around $19.70 ·
signature confirmation $3.95 online, adult signature $9.70.
A box labeled “Fine Jewelry Co.” is a higher-theft target than a plain brown box — the plain outer is a security decision, not a cost one.
Rates are published carrier guidance and re-check annually; the three-layer architecture does not change with rate updates.
